newsitem.title: USA: Albright endorses food aid to N. Korea.
newsitem.headline: Albright endorses food aid to N. Korea.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Wednesday endorsed U.S. food aid for North Korea to maintain stability in the Stalinist state.

"We...think that it is important to give some food assistance to North Korea through the World Food Programme because instability in North Korea is not to anybody's advantage," she told a congressional subsommittee.

The State Department said on Tuesday that the World Food Programme has formally appealed for $41.6 million in new food aid for North Korea and officials said the United States was certain to make a contribution.

Albright did not say how much additional aid the United States might contribute but experts have said Washington was expected to donate at least $8.425 million; South Korea, about $3 million, and Japan, about $6 million -- roughly the same as last year.

U.S. officials have acknowledged that the World Food Programme, a U.N. agency, had limited its appeal to only a fraction of North Korea's needs, estimated at 2.3 million tons. They say it would be impossible for the programme to meet all of the country's acute food needs, brought to a crisis by massive floods in 1995 and 1996. As a result, donations must be supplemented by commercial purchases by Pyongyang.

The United States has given Minneapolis-based grain giant Cargill Inc. a license to export 500,000 metric tons of foodstuffs to North Korea but Pyongyang and the company have been unable to strike a deal on financing.
